name: Burgenwelt Ehrenberg
kurzbeschreibung: Burgenwelt Ehrenberg near Reutte enchants as a monumental fortress complex featuring an interactive knight museum, castle ruins, and alpine scenery.
beschreibung:
Overview

Burgenwelt Ehrenberg, located south of the market town of Reutte, is one of Central Europe's most extensive and historically significant fortress complexes. Commanding the vital choke point of the ancient Via Claudia Augusta trade road, the site unites four interconnected fortifications: the medieval Ehrenberg Castle ruins, the baroque Schlosskopf citadel, Fort Claudia, and the valley defile fortification (Ehrenberger Klause). From the 13th to the 18th century, Ehrenberg served as the strategic gateway guarding northern Tyrol and controlling the lucrative salt transport routes. Today, the ensemble welcomes visitors with the immersive museum 'In the Footsteps of the Knight', fascinating open-air ramparts, and panoramic views stretching across the Reutte basin towards the Allgäu Alps.

Route & Requirements

Burgenwelt Ehrenberg offers tailored experiences for all ages and fitness levels. The valley hub at the Klause houses the visitor centre, the fully accessible knight museum, and welcoming restaurants. To reach the upper Ehrenberg ruins and Fort Claudia, visitors can hike well-graded gravel trails (roughly 30 minutes) or ascend smoothly aboard the modern Ehrenberg Liner funicular lift. Allow two to three hours to thoroughly appreciate the castle ruins, historical trails, and discovery stations. Sturdy walking shoes are recommended for exploring the stone ramparts and forest pathways.

Visiting & Getting There

The fortress is situated directly alongside the B179 Fernpass road just south of Reutte, featuring extensive car and coach parking at the base. Public transit passengers arrive via Reutte in Tirol railway station with connecting local buses dropping off directly at the 'Ehrenberger Klause' stop. The visitor centre and museum exhibition are open daily throughout the year. Access to the open-air castle grounds is free of charge, with tickets available for the museum, funicular lift, and suspension bridge.

Tips

Do not miss crossing the record-breaking highline179 suspension bridge, spanning 114 metres above the valley defile to connect Ehrenberg with Fort Claudia. Younger visitors love trying on authentic replica helmets and armour in the museum while solving interactive knightly riddles. In summer, the annual Ehrenberg Medieval Festival fills the grounds with jousting tournaments, period music, and vibrant artisan markets.
